timeline.text: Supper in the parlour; Colette serves and clears.
Ruth Marsh draws the fox first; Edmund keeps her sketchbooks and his silence.
Ruth Marsh's last sketchbook ends mid-page, one sentence pressed hard: 'H. carried the light away -- R.'
Ruth Marsh falls on the attic stair, on a storm-lit night. The house calls it a fall in the dark -- and the stair door was bolted from the landing side.
The last two Hollow books are drawn in Tobias Grimm's pencil under Edmund's signature -- and the forgeries Julian sold were traced and tea-aged in the attic.
Peggy retires with a novel and her sewing -- and the day's post: a final notice.
Julian Ashcombe arrives and repairs with Edmund to the study.
Raised voices behind the study door -- the argument over the sold sketches.
Edmund demands the money back. Julian writes a pencil plea -- pressed into the blotter.
Julian leaves by the front door. The ledger has it: 'gone quarter past ten.'
A cab takes Julian from the Bell & Curtain rank, away to Hall Lane. Gone before the dark.
Edmund bolts the study: seals the solicitor's letter, locks the carbon pages in the safe.
Edmund telephones someone for a few minutes. 'Come tonight. Bring nothing.'
Colette sets the morning's bread; kitchen door shut, wireless on.
Peggy comes down for her sewing scissors -- she was in the parlour after ten.
Lightning cuts the power; the hall clock stops. The house scatters for candles.
Colette lights the pantry lantern and bakes on in the dark; Peggy carries her candle up.
Peggy lights her bedside candle; it burns to the eleven-o'clock mark and no further.
Edmund shows his visitor the attic key: the sketchbooks go to the trust with Monday's preface.
Power returns; the hall clock restarts, twenty-one minutes blind. The kitchen wireless sings again to nobody.
The kitchen-garden door stands off its bolt. Someone used it in the dark.
The mantel clock falls and stops. Edmund staggers.
Edmund Vesper dies in the wing chair.
Colette brings the tea tray and finds him cold.
